transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brought me in is… my wife will be telling me things, like about my cousin’s appointments or who’s giving him a ride, and I’m looking right at her, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said. It’s been bothering me some.
Do you think you were paying attention to your wife when she was talking, but just couldn't remember what she said?

Yeah… I mean, I think I am paying attention. I’m looking right at her while she’s talking. But then a minute later, with stuff like my cousin’s appointments or who’s driving him, I realize I only caught part of it. Like it didn’t really sink in.
Does this happen only when your wife is talking to you, or do you also find it hard to take in information when you're reading or listening to other people?

It’s not just my wife. If I’m trying to go through notes for a catering order, or I’m on one of those parish planning calls, I’ll start out following it, but after a bit my mind drifts. Then I have to look back over the same notes like I didn’t really read them the first time.
Do you find yourself interested in the things you're trying to focus on, like the catering orders or the parish planning calls?

Some of it’s interesting enough, I guess. Like the catering stuff, I’m trying to focus on it. But if I sit down with an order, or I’m listening through a parish planning call, I’ll start off okay… then before long my mind kind of wanders. I end up going back over the same notes like I didn’t really read them.
Do you feel anxious, sad, or upset when you realize you haven't taken in the information?
I don’t know… not really sad or anything. Maybe a little frustrated with myself when it happens, but I mostly just try to go back and catch what I missed.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so… not in any big way. I still like the things I usually like, as far as I can tell.
Do you feel like these problems with taking in information are interfering with your daily life or causing you a lot of stress?

Yeah… I guess it is, a little. It’s caused some tension at home. My wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t really count on me with my cousin’s care sometimes.

And with the catering things, I’ve had to go back and double-check or redo small tasks so orders don’t get mixed up. It’s not… overwhelming, but it is getting in the way.
Do you ever find that you forget things that happened or conversations you had after some time has passed, not just immediately after?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. I might forget little details sometimes, but I haven’t noticed whole conversations or things just being gone later.
Do you feel like you're putting in enough effort to focus on the things you're trying to pay attention to?

I think I’m trying, yeah. It’s not like I’m not making an effort. If I sit down with a catering order or I’m listening on a parish planning call, I start out okay… but after a bit my mind drifts. Then I have to go back over the same notes, like I didn’t really take them in the first time.
Has anything particularly stressful or traumatic happened to you recently or in the past that might be contributing to your difficulty focusing?
Not traumatic, no. The main thing is… it’s been harder for about 11 months, since my cousin moved in with us after his surgery. That’s when I really started noticing it more.
Do you feel like you're not wanting to focus on these tasks, or is it more that you're trying to but your mind keeps drifting away?

It’s more that I’m trying, but my mind just kind of wanders off. Like with a catering order or a parish planning call, I’ll start out okay, and then after a while I realize I didn’t really take it in and have to go back over the notes.
Do you feel like you're not caring about the outcomes of the things you're trying to focus on, like the catering orders or parish planning calls?

No, I do care about how they turn out. It’s more… I’ll sit down with the order or the call notes and start off fine, but then my mind wanders. Then I’m looking back over the same notes like I didn’t really read them the first time.
Have you experienced any significant physical health changes or been diagnosed with any new medical conditions in the past year?
No… not that I can think of. I haven’t had any new diagnosis or big health change this past year.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past year?
Not really. I mean, nothing that stands out to me over the past year.
Do you ever feel like you're in a fog or dazed when you're trying to focus on something?

Kind of, yeah. Not dazed exactly, but I’ll start on a catering order or be listening to a parish planning call, and after a bit my mind’s just… somewhere else. Then I have to reread the same notes like I didn’t take them in.
Do you feel like you're in a fog when you're trying to focus, separate from your mind just wandering?
I’m not sure I’d call it a fog, exactly. It’s more like I just lose the thread. I don’t really notice feeling dazed or anything separate from that.
Do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself or your surroundings when your mind wanders?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, my attention drifts, but I still feel like I’m there. I wouldn’t say detached.
Do you feel like your difficulty focusing is related to feeling overwhelmed or stressed about your cousin living with you?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it being tied to that specifically. I mean, stress probably doesn’t help, but I don’t know that it’s because of my cousin being there.
Do you feel like you're not putting in enough effort to focus because you're just not motivated to do so?
I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’m just not trying. Sometimes I do try to focus and it still doesn’t really stick. Motivation might play a part sometimes, but… I’m not sure that’s the main thing.
Have you always had some difficulty focusing, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It’s not really new. I think it goes back pretty far. Even in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be daydreaming, leaving homework in my desk, needing reminders to finish classwork… things like that.
